title: no entity's authored prose can be edited after creation: issue bodies, issue titles and work package bodies all have write-once doors
body:
**THE CLASS, FILED ONCE, BECAUSE THREE PER-ENTITY NUMBERS ARE THREE RECORDS OF ONE DEFECT THAT DECAY INDEPENDENTLY.** Two members are already open and this row does not duplicate them -- it names what they are instances of, and it is the row a general fix closes.

**MEASURED 2026-08-30 by ic, driven against the debug binary.**

| entity | prose field | writing verbs | door |
| ------ | ----------- | ------------- | ---- |
| issue  | `body`      | `add` only, at creation      | none after creation -- `0090` |
| issue  | `title`     | `add` only, at creation      | none after creation -- `0151` |
| wp     | body        | `new` only, at creation      | **none -- this row** |

`intent wp` is `new`, `start`, `done`, `reopen`, `cancel`, `reinstate`, `unstart`, `rescope`, `list`, `show`. **Every one of those moves STATUS or SIZE; not one writes prose.** `intent issues` is `list`, `add`, `show`, `close`, `open` -- `add` takes `--body`/`--from` and allocates the number itself, so **no writing verb anywhere takes an id**, and an existing row cannot be addressed at all (measured by vc in a throwaway fixture, killing the hypothesis that `0131`'s upsert was an accidental update door).

**AND THE FILE IS NOT THE DOOR EITHER.** `intent/st/STxxxx/WP/NN/info.md` is a GENERATED view whose own footer says `Do not edit this file -- it is rendered from the model, and intent doctor reports any hand-edit as skew`. The store is the SSOT, so a hand-edit repairs the PROJECTION and leaves the SOURCE holding the thing that regenerates it -- this project has measured that a later status move is enough to restore what a hand-prune removed.

**THE LIVE CONSEQUENCE, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS NOT THEORETICAL.** `ST0064/WP-01`'s body specifies `GET /_status` returning JSON, carried from the Geodica handoff on 2026-08-26. hv ruled GraphQL three days later and `AC-01.3` supersedes it BY NAME. **The handoff IS the drop-in example, so a reader following the body lands on an endpoint that will not exist.** vc raised the correction and assigned it to ic; ic could not make it. **A superseded design that stays legible in the artefact is a design someone builds from**, and the correction is not merely undone -- it is unreachable through the surface, which turns a task into a blocked one.

**WHAT CLOSING IT REQUIRES.** An edit door reaching authored prose on an addressed entity -- at minimum `issues edit <id>` for title AND body, and a `wp` verb for the body. **A fix reaching only one field or only one entity closes the instance already filed and leaves the case that prompted the filing exactly where it is**, which is the shape this estate keeps meeting: a remedy sized to the instance rather than to the class.

**`0090` IS AN INSTANCE OF ITSELF AND CANNOT BE WIDENED TO COVER THIS.** It is titled *issues add creates a body that no verb can write*, it is OPEN, and **its own body is empty -- because no verb can write it.** So the register cannot describe its own gap in the row that names it, which is precisely why the class needs a row that is not one of its own victims. This one has a body because it was filed through `add --from`, at creation, which is the only door that exists.
